pr_title: Fix SetFeatureGateDuringTest handling of Parallel tests
pr_body:
/kind bug

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123677

```release-note
NONE
```

Test for ConsistentListFromCache feature flag were broken because they used t.Parallel(), which lead to **unpredictable incorrect setting of the feature flag**. As @wojtek-t is very set on not removing t.Parallel from cacher tests, I have implemented a proper fix to feature gates.

Wow, a lot of feature gate tests are broken.

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/5873433/2a0559a6-7f1e-41e4-9db0-f617fd725662)

> Wow, a lot of feature gate tests are broken.

a single test that called SetFeatureGateDuringTest serially would trip this detection but would not actually be broken:

```
defer SetFeatureGateDuringTest(..., false)()
... test stuff
defer SetFeatureGateDuringTest(..., true)()
... test more stuff
```
the first several "broken" tests I spot-checked are not actually broken, but would need to modify where / how they call SetFeatureGateDuringTest to avoid tripping this detection

a different way to detect specifically overlapping parallel uses would be to extract the calling goroutine ID (fragile, but ok in test-only code), and make sure SetFeatureGateDuringTest isn't called from a *different* goroutine until the cleanup is run

> > Wow, a lot of feature gate tests are broken.
> 
> a single test that called SetFeatureGateDuringTest serially would trip this detection but would not actually be broken:
> 
> ```
> defer SetFeatureGateDuringTest(..., false)()
> ... test stuff
> defer SetFeatureGateDuringTest(..., true)()
> ... test more stuff
> ```

Right, had different expecations that switching feature flag is set once per test.
Found one problematic test for now `TestSerializeObjectParallel`, the test was setting feature flag in parallel, but is not broken currently, as it was both enabled by default and set to true.
PTAL @liggitt

This doesn't actually "Fix SetFeatureGateDuringTest handling of Parallel tests" (title), does it? Calling `SetFeatureGateDuringTest` in parallel was risky before (only okay when done for different gates) and remains that way. It adds some detection of broken tests, but it doesn't fix some bug in SetFeatureGateDuringTest - at least that's what I gather from reading the diff.
it blocks the unsafe handling, and fails parallel tests that try to set the same gate, so in that sense, it fixes it :)

issue_context.title: SetFeatureGateDuringTest doesn't work if test is run in pararell.
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

`defer featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, features.ConsistentListFromCache, true)()` should change the feature flag to true, however feature flag is a global state, so if somewhere in the test we call `t.Parallel()` there is a risk that some other test changes the flag state in the mean time.

Found this when we launched broken ConsistentListFromCache to Alpha and only noticed issues in Beta as the test didn't really test anything. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123674/files#r1511492942.



### What did you expect to happen?

We should protect against usage of `featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest` and `t.Parallel` in a single test. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
func TestFeatureGateOn(t *testing.T) {
	defer featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, features.ConsistentListFromCache, true)()
	runFeatureGateTest(t, true)
}

func TestFeatureGateOff(t *testing.T) {
	defer featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, features.ConsistentListFromCache, false)()
	runFeatureGateTest(t, false)
}

func runFeatureGateTest(t *testing.T, expectEnabled bool) {
	t.Parallel()
	time.Sleep(time.Second)
	gotEnabled := utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate.Enabled(features.ConsistentListFromCache)
	if gotEnabled != expectEnabled {
		t.Errorf("unexpected feature gate state, got: %v, want: %v", gotEnabled, expectEnabled)
	}
}
```

Looks like issue doesn't appear when running on single CPU with `--cpu 1` flag.
In the watch cache tests we want to keep them running in parallel. The only way to prevent global state pollution is to move tests to separate files.

Yes, I think you are right because the feature gates are stored in a global variable (`utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate`). 
Maybe we could hack https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/hack/verify-test-featuregates.sh to detect such usage - although I'm not sure how easy it would be.

Tried one approach that didn't work. Wanted to prevent parallel calls to `SetFeatureGateDuringTest` by making the second caller wait until the first caller finishes. Unfortunately this doesn't work as it doesn't agree with how golang tests are parallelized. We don't have a guarantee (also cannot check that) that the caller is also parallelized and if it's not it will cause infinite block.

Looks like the best, but ugly way would be to separate tests setting the feature flag into different modules. Attempt:  
 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123701

> Looks like the best, but ugly way would be to separate tests setting the feature flag into different modules. Attempt:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123701

yes, I did something similar in the past when i wanted to make sure no other test will modify the global state - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/features/testing/features_init_test.go#L29

the alternative would be to get rid of the global state but that seems unfeasible as we would have to pass a feature gate implementation to every method that wants to use it.
